user: What is the process for managing volume spike protection and costs?
assistant: To manage volume spike protection and costs in IBM Log Analysis, you can follow these steps:
1. Configure index rates alerts: This helps you monitor and be alerted of unexpected spikes in your data volumes. The index rate can also be used to analyze and predict costs associated with storage of searchable data.
2. Calculate index rates: The index rates are calculated based on data that is ingested over the last 30 days and collected in 5 minute intervals. Data collection commences on January 31, 2022 for existing instances and from the day that the instance is provisioned for new instances. The standard hourly index rate is used to identify spikes or deviations in data volumes. The standard deviation is calculated by comparing the average hourly index rate with the average of the same hour over a rolling 30 day period. The severity of a spike is measured in standard deviations.
3. Use the z-score: The z-score represents the count of standard deviations and can be used to predict costs associated with storage of searchable data.
4. Control data usage: You can use the usage quota settings in your IBM Log Analysis instance to control how much data is stored. This helps you manage your data cost while still being able to view and retain the data that you need.
5. Utilize If you need to archive data, there is an API available for this purpose. The IP addresses used for the syslog-a.jp-tok.logging.cloud.ibm.com endpoint have changed if your service is configured to use specific IP addresses or firewall to a specific IP address, then modification to the new IP addresses will be required.
user: When data is archived can I still see the data?
assistant: Archived objects must be restored before you can access them. In an Activity Tracker instance, you can use the usage quota settings to control how much data is stored so you can manage your data cost while still being able to view and retain the data you need. To query the data, you can also use a service like SQL Query to query your COS archives and get information based on queries that you define. The Data Engine service provides a server-less, no-ETL solution to easily query data stored in Object Storage.

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
How and why do I configure index rate alerts?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
To configure index rate alerts in IBM Log Analysis, follow these steps:
1. Navigate to the web UI and select the settings icon.
2. In the Usage section, select Index Rate Alerts.
3. Enable the feature.
Once the feature is enabled, you can use the index rate alerts page to monitor the daily average index rates or the standard deviation from the past 30 days. You can toggle between viewing index rates or standard deviations for different time periods.
Configuring index rate alerts allows you to gain insight into which applications, sources, or tags produce data spikes, as well as any recently added sources. The alert message that is sent includes the top 20 sources and apps that have had the largest index rate growth in the past 2 hours, the list of the 20 newest sources added, and a link to download generated lists of all applications and sources.
Index rate alerts help you manage volume spike protection and costs by monitoring and controlling the number of log lines per second that are indexed and stored for search. They can also monitor for spikes on logs and anomalous flow rates.
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
Configure index rate alerts to identify which applications, sources, or tags are producing data spikes and to spot recently added sources. The feature is disabled by default; set at least one threshold to activate it. Alert messages include the 20 sources and apps with the largest index-rate growth in the past 2 hours, the 20 newest sources, and a link to download full lists of applications and sources. Notifications continue until the index rate falls below your configured thresholds. You can also choose which days and hours alerts are sent, and individual recipients can mute alert emails. (第1页)
[The End of Assistant's Answer]

By default the index rate alert feature is disabled.

When you configure index rate alerts, you can gain insight into which applications, sources, or tags produce data spikes, as well as any recently added sources. The alert message that is sent includes the following information:



* The top 20 sources and apps that have had the largest index rate growth in the past 2 hours.
* The list of the 20 newest sources added.
* A link to download generated lists of all applications and sources.

Notifications are sent until the index rate reports a value that is below the thresholds that you have configured.

Individual recipients may mute alert emails.

You can also configure a custom schedule to set the days and hours that you want alerts to be send if the thresholds are exceeded.
